metadata.title: A constructive proof of the general Lovász Local Lemma
metadata.authors: Robin A. Moser and Gábor Tardos
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Dependency graph $G_{\mathcal{A}}$
nodes.statement: For a family $\mathcal{A}$ of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$, the dependency graph $G = G_{\mathcal{A}}$ has vertex set $\mathcal{A}$ with an edge between $A,B$ iff $A \neq B$ and $\mathrm{vbl}(A) \cap \mathrm{vbl}(B) \neq \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph on events with edges between events sharing a determining variable.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{vbl}(A)$ and inclusive neighborhood $\Gamma^{+}(A)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{vbl}(A)$ is the unique minimal subset $S \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ that determines $A$. The inclusive neighborhood is $\Gamma^{+}(A) := \Gamma(A) \cup \{A\}$.

nodes.name: Witness tree
nodes.statement: A witness tree $\tau = (T, \sigma_T)$ is a finite rooted tree $T$ with a labelling $\sigma_T : V(T) \to \mathcal{A}$ such that the children of any vertex $u$ receive labels from $\Gamma^{+}(\sigma_T(u))$. It is proper if distinct children of the same vertex receive distinct labels.

nodes.name: Execution log $C$ and $\tau_C(t)$
nodes.statement: The log $C : \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{A}$ records the event resampled at each step. The witness tree $\tau_C(t)$ is built by initializing $\tau_C^{(t)}(t)$ as a root labelled $C(t)$ and going backwards: for $i = t-1,\ldots,1$, if some vertex $v$ has $C(i) \in \Gamma^{+}([v])$, attach a new child labelled $C(i)$ to a maximum-depth such $v$.

nodes.name: Lopsidependence and lopsidependency graph
nodes.statement: Two events $A,B \in \mathcal{A}$ are lopsidependent if there exist evaluations $f,g$ that differ only on $\mathrm{vbl}(A) \cap \mathrm{vbl}(B)$ such that $f$ violates $A$ and $g$ violates $B$, but either $f$ does not violate $B$ or $g$ does not violate $A$. The lopsidependency graph has edges between lopsidependent events; $\Gamma'(A)$ is the neighborhood in this graph.

nodes.name: Elementary event
nodes.statement: An event $A \in \mathcal{A}$ is elementary if there is a single evaluation of the variables in $\mathrm{vbl}(A)$ violating $A$.

nodes.name: Consistency of witness tree with evaluation sequences
nodes.statement: A witness tree $\tau$ is consistent with sequences $(v_i^{(j)})_{i,j}$ if the $\tau$-check passes when these sequences are substituted for the random source.

nodes.name: Lovász Local Lemma (general form)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set of events. For $A \in \mathcal{A}$ let $\Gamma(A) \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ such that $A$ is independent of $\mathcal{A} \setminus (\{A\} \cup \Gamma(A))$. If there is $x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)} (1 - x(B))$ for all $A$, then $\Pr[\bigcap_A \bar{A}] \geq \prod_A (1 - x(A)) > 0$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ finite set of events in a probability space
$A$ independent of $\mathcal{A} \setminus (\{A\} \cup \Gamma(A))$ for each $A$
$\exists\, x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$

nodes.name: Constructive LLL via sequential resampling
nodes.statement: Under the LLL hypothesis with variable-determined events, the sequential resampling algorithm finds a non-violating assignment, with $\mathbb{E}[N_A] \leq x(A)/(1-x(A))$ resamplings of each $A$ and total expected steps at most $\sum_{A} x(A)/(1-x(A))$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P}$ finite set of mutually independent random variables
$\mathcal{A}$ finite set of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$
$\exists\, x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma_{\mathcal{A}}(A)} (1-x(B))$
conclusions: There exists an assignment to $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$
Algorithm 1.1 resamples each $A$ at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ times in expectation

nodes.name: Parallel LLL bound
nodes.statement: Under the slightly strengthened hypothesis $\Pr[A] \leq (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)} (1-x(B))$ with $\varepsilon > 0$, the parallel algorithm takes expected $O\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} \log \sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A))\bigr)$ steps.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P}$ finite set of mutually independent random variables
$\mathcal{A}$ finite set of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$
$\varepsilon > 0$ and $\exists\, x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma_{\mathcal{A}}(A)} (1-x(B))$
conclusions: Parallel algorithm (Algorithm 1.2) terminates in expected $O\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} \log \sum_{A} \tfrac{x(A)}{1-x(A)}\bigr)$ steps

nodes.name: Deterministic LLL under bounded degree
nodes.statement: Suppose conditional probabilities $\Pr[A \mid \forall i \in I : P_i = v_i]$ can be computed in $\mathrm{poly}(s)$ time, the dependency graph has maximum degree $\leq k$ (constant), and $\Pr[A] \leq (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$. Then a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm finds a non-violating assignment.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P} = \{P_1,\ldots,P_n\}$ each $P_i$ over finite domain $D_i$
$\mathcal{A}$ has $m$ events; problem size $s := m + n + \sum_i |D_i|$
Conditional probability oracle in $\mathrm{poly}(s)$
$|\Gamma_{\mathcal{A}}(A)| \leq k$ for a constant $k$
$\exists\, \varepsilon > 0$ constant and $x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$
conclusions: A deterministic algorithm finds an evaluation of $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in time $\mathrm{poly}(s)$

nodes.name: Lopsided constructive LLL
nodes.statement: If $\Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma'_{\mathcal{A}}(A)} (1-x(B))$ for $x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$, then the randomized algorithm finds a non-violating assignment, resampling each $A$ at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ times in expectation.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P}$ finite set of mutually independent random variables
$\mathcal{A}$ finite set of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$
$\exists\, x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma'_{\mathcal{A}}(A)}(1-x(B))$
conclusions: There exists an assignment to $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$
Algorithm 1.1 resamples each $A$ at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ times in expectation

nodes.name: Properness and probability bound for witness trees
nodes.statement: Let $\tau$ be a fixed witness tree and $C$ the random log. (i) If $\tau$ occurs in $C$, then $\tau$ is proper. (ii) The probability that $\tau$ appears in $C$ is at most $\prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \Pr[[v]]$.
assumptions: $\tau$ is a fixed witness tree
$C$ is the random log produced by the sequential algorithm
conclusions: (i) If $\tau$ occurs in $C$, then $\tau$ is proper

nodes.name: Galton-Watson probability of a witness tree
nodes.statement: Let $x'(B) := x(B) \prod_{C \in \Gamma(B)} (1-x(C))$. For a proper witness tree $\tau$ with root labelled $A$, the probability that the multitype Galton–Watson process yields exactly $\tau$ is $p_\tau = \frac{1-x(A)}{x(A)} \prod_{v \in V(\tau)} x'([v])$.
assumptions: $\tau$ proper witness tree with root labelled $A$
Galton–Watson branching process as defined in Section 3
$x'(B) := x(B) \prod_{C \in \Gamma(B)} (1-x(C))$

nodes.name: Witness tree depth equals parallel step index minus one
nodes.statement: If $t \in S_j$, where $S_j$ is the segment of the sequentialized log corresponding to step $j$ of the parallel algorithm, then the depth of $\tau_C(t)$ equals $j - 1$.
assumptions: Execution of parallel algorithm sequentialized into log $C$
$S_j$ the segment of $C$ from parallel step $j$
$t \in S_j$

nodes.name: Bounded-size consistent witness tree exists
nodes.statement: If the dependency graph has max degree $\leq k$ and there exists a consistent witness tree of size $\geq u$, then there is also a consistent witness tree of some size in $[u, (k+1)u]$.
assumptions: Maximum degree of dependency graph bounded by $k$
$u \in \mathbb{N}$
Exists witness tree of size $\geq u$ consistent with given evaluation sequences $(v_i^{(j)})$
conclusions: Exists witness tree of some size in $[u, (k+1)u]$ consistent with the sequences

nodes.name: Probability bound for lopsided witness trees
nodes.statement: For a fixed proper lopsided witness tree $\tau$ and the random log $C$ of the algorithm, $\Pr[\exists t : \varrho_C(t) = \tau] \leq \prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \Pr[[v]]$.
assumptions: $\tau$ proper lopsided witness tree
$C$ random log of Algorithm 1.1

nodes.name: Sequential solver (Algorithm 1.1)
nodes.statement: Randomized resampling algorithm: initialize variables randomly, then repeatedly pick an arbitrary violated event $A$ and resample the variables in $\mathrm{vbl}(A)$ until no event is violated.
input: Set $\mathcal{P}$ of mutually independent random variables
Set $\mathcal{A}$ of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$ (with $\mathrm{vbl}(A)$ accessible)
output: An evaluation $(v_P)_{P \in \mathcal{P}}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$

nodes.name: Parallel solver (Algorithm 1.2)
nodes.statement: Parallel variant: in each round, pick a maximal independent set $S$ of currently violated events in $G_{\mathcal{A}}$ and resample the variables in $\bigcup_{A \in S} \mathrm{vbl}(A)$ in parallel.
input: Set $\mathcal{P}$ of mutually independent random variables
output: An evaluation $(v_P)_{P \in \mathcal{P}}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$

nodes.name: Deterministic LLL solver
nodes.statement: Derandomized variant: enumerate witness trees of size in $[c \log m, (k+1) c \log m]$, then use the method of conditional expectations to fix variable samples $v_i^{(j)}$ ($1 \leq i \leq n$, $0 \leq j \leq c \log m$) so no large consistent witness tree exists; then run sequential algorithm on the fixed sequences.
input: Constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and $x$ as in Theorem 1.4 hypothesis
output: An evaluation of $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$, found in time $\mathrm{poly}(s)$

nodes.name: $\tau$-check
nodes.statement: Auxiliary procedure: visit vertices of $\tau$ in non-increasing depth order; for each vertex $v$ draw fresh random samples for $\mathrm{vbl}([v])$ and check whether $[v]$ is violated. The check passes if all events were violated when checked.
input: An infinite list of random samples $P^{(0)}, P^{(1)}, \ldots$ for each $P \in \mathcal{P}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1 (witness tree properness and probability)
nodes.statement: Coupling argument: if $\tau = \tau_C(t)$, run a $\tau$-check on the same random source; show labels at each depth form an independent set (giving properness) and that the $\tau$-check passes whenever $\tau$ occurs in $C$ (giving the probability bound).

nodes.name: Depth-monotonicity for shared variables
nodes.statement: Show that if $q(u) < q(v)$ and $\mathrm{vbl}([u]) \cap \mathrm{vbl}([v]) \neq \emptyset$ then $d(u) > d(v)$, by tracing the witness-tree construction at step $q(u)+1$.

nodes.name: Independence at each level $\Rightarrow$ properness
nodes.statement: Conclude that vertices at the same depth carry events with disjoint $\mathrm{vbl}$, so labels at each level form an independent set in $G_{\mathcal{A}}$; in particular $\tau$ is proper, establishing (i).

nodes.name: Define $\tau$-check and its probability
nodes.statement: Introduce the $\tau$-check and observe that it passes with probability exactly $\prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \Pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Coupling: occurrence in log $\Rightarrow$ $\tau$-check passes
nodes.statement: Couple algorithm and $\tau$-check to a shared random source $P^{(0)}, P^{(1)},\ldots$; show that when the algorithm samples $P$ at step $q(v)$ the value used is $P^{(|S(P)|)}$, the same value the $\tau$-check uses, so $[v]$ is violated for the $\tau$-check too.

nodes.name: Conclude probability bound (ii)
nodes.statement: Since $\tau$ occurs in $C$ implies the $\tau$-check passes, $\Pr[\tau \text{ in } C] \leq \Pr[\tau\text{-check passes}] = \prod_{v} \Pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1 (Galton-Watson probability)
nodes.statement: Compute $p_\tau$ by writing the product over vertices of $\tau$ of birth probabilities $x([v])$ and non-birth probabilities $1 - x([u])$ for $u \in W_v$; rewrite over $\Gamma^{+}([v])$ and simplify to obtain $\frac{1-x(A)}{x(A)} \prod_v x'([v])$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Bound $\mathbb{E}[N_A] \leq \sum_{\tau \in T_A} \Pr[\tau \text{ in } C]$ by Lemma 2.1; substitute the assumption to get $\sum_{\tau} \prod_v x'([v])$; rewrite as $\frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)} \sum_\tau p_\tau$ via Lemma 3.1; bound the Galton–Watson sum by $1$.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathbb{E}[N_A]$ by sum over witness trees
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[N_A] = \sum_{\tau \in T_A} \Pr[\tau \text{ in } C] \leq \sum_{\tau \in T_A} \prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \Pr[[v]]$ via Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Apply LLL hypothesis
nodes.statement: Substitute $\Pr[A] \leq x'([v])$ via the assumption: $\sum_{\tau} \prod_v \Pr[[v]] \leq \sum_\tau \prod_v x'([v])$.

nodes.name: Rewrite via Galton-Watson identity
nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.1, $\sum_\tau \prod_v x'([v]) = \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)} \sum_\tau p_\tau \leq \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)}$ since $\sum_\tau p_\tau \leq 1$ (Galton-Watson process produces at most one tree).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Backwards induction on parallel step $k$: $\tau_k$ is obtained from $\tau_{k+1}$ by attaching vertices at depth one greater. If a max-depth vertex of $\tau_{k+1}$ has no Γ$^{+}$-neighbor resampled in step $k$, that event was already violated, contradicting maximality of $S$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: Let $Q(k) = \Pr[\text{parallel runs} \geq k \text{ steps}]$. By Lemma 4.1, some witness tree of depth $k-1$ (hence size $\geq k$) occurs. Bound $Q(k) \leq (1-\varepsilon)^k \sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A))$, which yields the logarithmic bound on expected steps.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Assume $\tau$ is a smallest counterexample of size $> (k+1)u$. Build $j \leq k+1$ smaller consistent witness trees $\tau_i$ from the children of the root; at least one has size $\geq (|\tau|-1)/(k+1) \geq u$, contradicting either the assumption or minimality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4 (derandomization)
nodes.statement: Replace $x$ by $\tilde{x}(A) = (1-\varepsilon/2) x(A)$ to bound weights. Show expected number of consistent witness trees of size $\geq c \log m$ is $\leq 1/2$; enumerate trees of bounded size using Lemma 5.1; greedily fix $v_i^{(j)}$ via conditional expectations to keep this expectation $\leq 1/2$ until it must be zero.

nodes.name: Bound weights away from $1$
nodes.statement: Replace $x(A)$ by $\tilde{x}(A) := (1 - \varepsilon/2) x(A)$ and $\varepsilon$ by $\varepsilon/2$ to ensure weights $\leq 1 - \varepsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Expected number of large consistent trees is small
nodes.statement: Show expected number of consistent witness trees of size $\geq k$ is $\leq (1-\varepsilon)^k \sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A)) = O(m(1-\varepsilon)^k)$, so for $k = c \log m$ this is $\leq 1/2$.

nodes.name: Enumerate bounded-size trees via Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 5.1 to argue that it suffices to enumerate witness trees of size in $[c \log m, (k+1) c \log m]$; this list $L$ has polynomial length under bounded degree.

nodes.name: Method of conditional expectations on $v_i^{(j)}$
nodes.statement: Greedily fix $v_i^{(j)}$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$, $0 \leq j \leq c \log m$ to keep expected number of consistent trees $\leq 1/2$; once all values fixed the expectation equals an integer, hence $0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.2 (lopsided coupling)
nodes.statement: Couple algorithm and $\tau$-check via shared random samples; among logs $C$ with $\varrho_C(t) = \tau$ pick the one minimizing $w(C)$; show that under lopsidependence this enforces $q_C(v_i) = i$, so the $\tau$-check passes.

nodes.name: LLL inequality
nodes.statement: $\forall A \in \mathcal{A} : \Pr[A] \leq x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)} (1 - x(B))$

nodes.name: Slack-LLL inequality (parallel/derandomization)
nodes.statement: $\forall A \in \mathcal{A} : \Pr[A] \leq (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma_{\mathcal{A}}(A)} (1 - x(B))$

nodes.name: Modified weight $x'(B)$
nodes.statement: $x'(B) := x(B) \prod_{C \in \Gamma(B)} (1 - x(C))$

nodes.name: Hypergraph $2$-coloring (Beck's setting)
nodes.statement: Beck's hypergraph $2$-coloring example: every edge contains $\geq k$ vertices and shares vertices with $\leq 2^{k/48}$ other edges; existential LLL allows $\leq 2^k/e$, and successive papers raised the algorithmic threshold (Alon $2^{k/8}$; Srinivasan $2^{k/4}$; Moser $2^{k/2}$; Moser $2^k/32$).

nodes.name: SAT with bounded-occurrence variables (lopsidependence)
nodes.statement: In CNF formulas, two clauses are in conflict if one contains literal $\ell$ and the other $\bar{\ell}$; the events that they are violated are lopsidependent. Berman, Karpinski, Scott [BKS03] used the lopsided LLL for better bounds on number of variable occurrences.

nodes.name: Tightness of $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ bound
nodes.statement: The bound $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ in Theorem 1.2 is tight only in the trivial case where $A$ is isolated in the dependency graph and $x(A) = \Pr[A]$; the total bound is tight only when all events are independent.

nodes.name: Implementation requirements and Luby's algorithm
nodes.statement: The sequential version requires only sampling and violation-detection oracles. The parallel version additionally needs maximal independent set computation, e.g. via Luby's randomized algorithm in $O(\log m)$ expected time per round, yielding $O(\log^2 m)$ total.

nodes.name: Derandomization without bounded degree
nodes.statement: Is it possible to derandomize the algorithm even when the degrees of the dependency graph are unbounded?

nodes.name: Analysis of single-step Luby variant
nodes.statement: If a single Luby step is used (in lieu of a maximal independent set) for parallel resampling, what is the expected number of rounds until termination?

nodes.name: Effective parallelization of the lopsided LLL
nodes.statement: The authors note they could not find an effective parallelization of the lopsided generalization (Theorem 6.1).
